phenotype_specificity.statement: Infantile- or childhood-onset fever with severe colitis and mucosal ulcers in both reports. 40859316 reports negative autoantibody, pathogen and skin prick tests (patient-level table). 41890736 Patient 1 also has motor and cognitive developmental delay, which the paper does not explain. Neither paper reports other candidate variants for this person.

quotes.quote: Autoantibody panels, rheumatoid factor, skin prick test and pathogen screening were negative.
| Motor and cognitive development delay | YES | NO | NO | NO | YES |

segregation.statement: not reported (no affected relatives; 41890736 reports no family history for any patient)

quotes.quote: None of the patients reported a family history of genetic disorders or any special allergies.

de_novo.statement: 40859316: both parents tested by WES with Sanger validation and had wild-type genotypes. 41890736: all variants stated de novo after parental testing. Parentage confirmation is not reported in either paper.

quotes.quote: C WES for Patient 1 and her parents. A heterozygous TNFAIP3 mutation (c.866delA) was identified in the proband, while both parents exhibited wild-type genotypes
were classified as pathogenic per ACMG criteria and confirmed as de novo via parental testing (Fig. 5).
All patients were de novo (they have all been tested to confirm their origin).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Single-nucleotide deletion predicted to cause a frameshift (p.(His289ProfsTer3)) in the OTU domain. 40859316 says it removes all zinc-finger domains and attributes the disease to loss of A20 function.

quotes.quote: This highly pathogenic frameshift mutation disrupts part of the OTU domain and causes complete loss of all zinc finger domains (ZnFs).
Loss of A20 function disrupts this regulatory balance, leading to unchecked NF-κB activation and predisposing individuals to autoimmune and autoinflammatory disorders [12, 13].

concerns: POSSIBLE SAME PERSON: HA20-ID0382 and HA20-ID0433 are both girls with de novo c.866delA from the same region (Children's Hospital Affiliated to Zhengzhou University, 2015-2024; Henan Children's Hospital, 2019-2023). 41890736 lists its Patient 1 apart from 'the case reported by Xue et al' (40859316) and gives different features (genital ulcers NO vs YES; developmental delay YES vs NO). Onset also differs (11 months vs 'five years' in 41890736's discussion).

Evidence that the two series overlap: 41890736 Patient 4 (c.133C>T, female, 10 m) and 40859316 Patient 3 (c.133C>T, female, onset 10 months) have identical laboratory values (WBC 13.41, Hb 94.2, PLT 454, CRP 108.54, ESR 19). At least one child appears in both papers, which raises the chance that the c.866delA carriers are one child too.

41890736 contains internal inconsistencies: MMACHC variants are given to patient 3 in the abstract and discussion but to patient 2 in the Figure 1 legend and treatment text, and its Table 3 labels the c.133C>T case 'Patient 3' although that variant belongs to Patient 4. Its patient-level data should be read with care.
Transcripts differ: NM_006290.4 (40859316) and NM_006290.5 (41890736), not the batch's NM_001270508.2. The protein positions agree.
notes_for_panel: If the two identities are one person, this is a single de novo case, not two.
